config.title: Theme Context

intro.title: Theme Context
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a theme switcher that allows users to toggle between light and dark modes in a React application. You'll learn how to use React Context to manage and share theme state across multiple components without prop drilling. The main technologies involved are React's Context API, TypeScript for type safety, and custom hooks for clean consumption. By the end, you'll understand how to create a context provider, define theme types, and access theme values anywhere in your component tree.
intro.usecase: Theme Context is essential for implementing consistent dark/light mode across entire applications, like in productivity tools (Notion, Slack) or developer dashboards (GitHub, Vercel). It allows users to toggle themes that instantly apply to all components—navigation bars, side panels, modals, and form inputs—without prop drilling. This pattern also supports accessibility by maintaining high contrast settings and custom color schemes in enterprise applications. Developers use Theme Context to manage design tokens centrally, ensuring UI consistency while simplifying maintenance.

objectives: Apply the createContext function from React to initialize a ThemeContext for managing theme state.
Define a ThemeProvider component that wraps children and controls theme data flow.
Implement useState to store and update the current theme value within the provider.
Construct a custom hook (useTheme) to access theme context values in child components.
Utilize the useContext hook to retrieve theme data from the nearest ThemeProvider.
Execute conditional rendering based on theme state to apply different CSS classes or styles.
Modify theme state through handler functions that toggle between light and dark modes.
Assign default theme values and TypeScript types to ensure type safety across the context.
Control component behavior by passing theme state and update functions through context value.
Access theme context in multiple components to demonstrate centralized state management.
Return appropriate JSX structure from the ThemeProvider that renders children with context.
Handle theme changes by wiring UI elements (buttons, toggles) to context update functions.

steps.title: Import React and createContext from 'react'
steps.instruction: Import React and the createContext function from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and createContext from the same package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing React and createContext
import React, { createContext } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React and createContext from 'react' here
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have an import statement that brings in both React and createContext from the 'react' package.
successCriteria: The code must include a valid import statement for React and createContext from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and createContext. This gives you access to React's core functionality and the ability to create context objects.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check your import syntax. Make sure you're importing both React and createContext from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import both React and createContext from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Import useState and useContext from 'react'
steps.instruction: Import the useState and useContext hooks from the 'react' package. Add the import statement below the existing imports.
steps.hint: Use named imports from 'react' to bring in both hooks.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing useState and useContext from 'react'
import { useState, useContext } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The code will have both useState and useContext imported alongside React and createContext.
successCriteria: The import statement should include both useState and useContext from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported both useState and useContext hooks. These will be essential for managing state and consuming context in your theme implementation.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both useState and useContext from the 'react' package in the same import statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to import both useState and useContext from the 'react' package. Check that your import statement uses the correct syntax and includes both hooks.

steps.title: Define Theme type
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript type called 'Theme' that can only have the string literal values 'light' or 'dark'.
steps.hint: Use the 'type' keyword to create a union type of string literals.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of defining a type with string literal values
type Status = 'active' | 'inactive' | 'pending';
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a type definition for Theme that restricts its values to 'light' or 'dark'.
successCriteria: The code must include a type definition named 'Theme' with union type 'light' | 'dark'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the Theme type. This will help ensure our theme values are type-safe throughout the app.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the Theme type definition needs adjustment. Make sure it's a union type that only allows 'light' or 'dark' as values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Theme type definition is missing or incorrect. You need to create a type called 'Theme' that can only be 'light' or 'dark'.

steps.title: Create ThemeContext with createContext
steps.instruction: Create a ThemeContext using the createContext function you imported. Pass undefined as the initial value and export it.
steps.hint: Use createContext<Theme | undefined>(undefined) to create a context that can hold either a Theme object or undefined.
steps.expectedOutcome: A ThemeContext variable is created and exported, ready to be used as a context provider and consumer.
successCriteria: The context type is Theme | undefined
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a ThemeContext with the correct type and initial value.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using createContext with the correct type (Theme | undefined) and initial value (undefined), and that you export it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ThemeContext wasn't created correctly. Remember to use createContext<Theme | undefined>(undefined) and export it.

steps.title: Create ThemeProvider component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ThemeProvider that takes children as props. The component should return children wrapped in the ThemeContext.Provider.
steps.hint: Define a component that accepts a children prop and returns ThemeContext.Provider with children as its content.
steps.expectedOutcome: A ThemeProvider component is defined that will later provide the theme value to its children.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the ThemeProvider component. This component will serve as the wrapper that provides theme context to all its children.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your component: 1) is named ThemeProvider, 2) accepts a children prop, 3) returns ThemeContext.Provider, and 4) wraps children inside it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ThemeProvider component wasn't created correctly. Please create a functional component named ThemeProvider that takes children as props and returns ThemeContext.Provider wrapping those children.

steps.title: Initialize theme state in ThemeProvider
steps.instruction: Inside the ThemeProvider component, initialize a state variable named 'theme' using useState, with a default value of 'light'.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. Remember to specify the type as 'Theme'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of initializing state with useState
const [theme, setTheme] = useState<Theme>('light');
steps.expectedOutcome: The ThemeProvider component now has a state variable 'theme' initialized to 'light', ready to be provided through the context.
successCriteria: The code should include a useState call inside ThemeProvider that declares a variable named 'theme' with the type 'Theme' and initial value 'light'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the theme state inside ThemeProvider. This state will hold the current theme value that can be shared through context.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but there's something missing. Make sure you're using useState with the correct type annotation for Theme and initializing it to 'light'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Remember to use the useState hook inside the ThemeProvider component to create a state variable named 'theme' with type 'Theme' and initial value 'light'.

steps.title: Create toggleTheme handler
steps.instruction: Inside your ThemeProvider component, define a function named toggleTheme that switches the theme state between 'light' and 'dark'.
steps.hint: Create a function that uses the setTheme setter from useState to update the theme based on its current value.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a toggleTheme function that toggles the theme between 'light' and 'dark' when called.
successCriteria: The toggleTheme function must be defined inside ThemeProvider and use setTheme to update the theme based on its current value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a toggleTheme function that switches between light and dark themes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a toggleTheme function, but it might not correctly toggle between 'light' and 'dark'. Make sure it uses setTheme to update based on the current theme value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggleTheme function is missing or doesn't properly toggle the theme. Remember to define it inside ThemeProvider and use setTheme to switch between 'light' and 'dark'.

steps.title: Return ThemeContext.Provider with value
steps.instruction: Inside your ThemeProvider component, return the ThemeContext.Provider component with a value prop that contains an object with both the current theme and the toggleTheme function.
steps.hint: The value prop should be an object with properties 'theme' and 'toggleTheme' that reference the existing state and handler.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ThemeProvider component now returns a ThemeContext.Provider that makes the theme state and toggle function available to all child components.
successCriteria: The component returns ThemeContext.Provider with a value prop containing an object with 'theme' and 'toggleTheme' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully returned the ThemeContext.Provider with the theme state and toggle function in the value object. This makes them available to all components that consume this context.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're returning ThemeContext.Provider with a value prop that contains an object with both 'theme' and 'toggleTheme' properties. Check that you're using the existing theme state and toggleTheme function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ThemeProvider component should return ThemeContext.Provider with a value prop containing an object with 'theme' and 'toggleTheme' properties. Remember to use the existing theme state and toggleTheme function you defined earlier.

steps.title: Create useTheme custom hook
steps.instruction: Define a custom hook named 'useTheme' that uses useContext with ThemeContext to access the theme context value.
steps.hint: Create a function that calls useContext with ThemeContext as the argument and returns the result.
steps.expectedOutcome: A custom hook named useTheme is created that uses useContext to access ThemeContext.
successCriteria: The code should define a function named 'useTheme' that calls 'useContext(ThemeContext)' and returns the result.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the useTheme custom hook. This hook will allow components to easily access the theme context value.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're creating a function named 'useTheme' that uses useContext with ThemeContext as the argument and returns the value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The custom hook wasn't created correctly. You need to define a function named 'useTheme' that calls useContext with ThemeContext and returns the result.

steps.title: Create main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns a JSX element.
steps.hint: Define a component function called App that returns a JSX element (like a div).
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and ready to be used as the main entry point.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main App component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you define a component named App that returns JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component is not correctly defined. Create a function named App that returns JSX.

steps.title: Use useTheme hook in App component
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, call the useTheme hook to get the theme and toggleTheme values.
steps.hint: Call the useTheme hook and destructure the returned object to get theme and toggleTheme.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have access to the theme and toggleTheme values from the context via the useTheme hook.
successCriteria: The App component should call useTheme and destructure theme and toggleTheme from the returned object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully used the useTheme hook to access the theme context values in your App component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling useTheme and destructuring both theme and toggleTheme from the returned object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component should call the useTheme hook to get the theme and toggleTheme values. Try calling useTheme and destructuring the returned object.

steps.title: Return JSX with theme display and toggle button
steps.instruction: In the App component, return JSX that displays the current theme value and a button that calls toggleTheme when clicked.
steps.hint: Use the theme variable from useTheme to display the current theme. Add a button with an onClick handler that calls toggleTheme.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will display the current theme value and a button that toggles between light and dark themes when clicked.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully displayed the current theme and wired the toggle button. The App component now shows the theme state and allows the user to toggle it.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're displaying the theme value and the button has an onClick handler that calls toggleTheme.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component doesn't yet display the theme or have a working toggle button. Check that you're using the theme variable from useTheme and wiring the button's onClick to toggleTheme.
